A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Interact-RAG work. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, figures, and tables are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original QA benchmark results, training and interaction ablations, training dynamics, and a retrieval case study.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds news-domain evaluation, component ablations, retrieval-quality measurements, computational-cost comparisons, and other diagnostics.

M1.justification: The interaction primitives, planner-reasoner-executor workflow, SFT/GRPO training, and reward function remain unchanged. Added descriptions of RL token masking, normalization, filter persistence, and execution order disclose implementation details without establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix C.2 adds evaluation on MultiHop-RAG, extending the previously Wikipedia-based coverage to news covering technology, health, and business. This materially broadens domain coverage; the original six benchmarks and training datasets remain.

E2.justification: The main benchmark comparator set is retained. v2 adds RRF and CombMNZ as fusion alternatives in Table 8 and a Search-R1 best-of-three variant in Appendix C.4, providing limited additional comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 substantially expands evaluation beyond answer accuracy and turn counts: supporting-fact coverage, latency, tool time, token consumption, memory, and best-of-three testing are added. New cost experiments specify Qwen2.5-7B with A100/vLLM, while engine testing uses eight CPU cores and 96 concurrent clients. Existing core evaluation settings are retained.

E4.justification: Table 3 newly isolates the three interaction components. Appendices C.3-C.6 investigate retrieved-evidence coverage, cost versus accuracy, fusion sensitivity, and engine overhead, including a best-of-three control. Appendix D.3 adds training-format error diagnostics. These substantially extend the earlier aggregate ablations, training analyses, and case study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run variability, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Best-of-three sampling in v2 is an inference control, not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: All original main benchmark scores are preserved, including average EM scores of 52.8 for 8B and 47.5 for 7B. Substantial new results include MultiHop-RAG EM scores of 79.4/81.4 for 7B/8B, component and fusion comparisons, evidence coverage, and cost measurements. Table 7 newly reports 36.4-second latency for Interact-RAG-7B versus 17.2 seconds for Search-R1-7B.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 adds the mathematical observation that the constant -1 reward offset cancels during GRPO group normalization and cannot affect advantages or training, qualifying the earlier penalty rationale. The objective and reward equations themselves remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same interaction paradigm, reasoning workflow, two-stage training contributions, and headline 22.5% relative improvement. Added experiments support these retained claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly distinguishes fewer retrieval iterations from higher total latency and token use, adding a substantive cost trade-off and limitations discussion. It also discusses outcome-reward limitations, dataset-dependent component contributions, and why gains may reflect interaction quality rather than simply larger retrieved contexts.

D1.justification: v2 specifies min-max normalization, entity-term normalization, filter reissuing, concurrent-action execution order, and RL token masking. It also documents settings for the added cost tests and states that source code accompanies supplementary materials. These fill reproducibility gaps; the existing training hyperparameters, hardware, corpus construction, and prompts largely remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including MultiHop-RAG, reciprocal rank fusion, proactive multi-agent information seeking, Towards AI Search Paradigm, RankElectra, and RankExpert. The related-work narrative and positioning against black-box retrieval remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The original narrative largely survives, with localized rewriting, spelling corrections, an experimental-settings subsection, ethics/reproducibility statements, and reorganized appendices including limitations. Some cross-references deteriorate, notably the unresolved 'Table ??' and references to 'Table 4.3'.

P2.justification: v2 merges the original main and appendix backbone evaluations into an expanded main Table 1 and adds five tables for new evaluations. The training-free table drops parenthetical percentage decreases, Figure 3 receives a more precise caption, and Figure 5 changes bar styling. The original plotted findings and case study are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for the retrieval mechanism through component ablations, supporting-fact coverage, and a non-Wikipedia evaluation. It also resolves an important omission in v1's efficiency discussion by measuring latency and token costs and acknowledging their trade-off with accuracy. These gains in empirical substantiation and transparency outweigh localized cross-reference defects, although uncertainty estimates remain absent.
